source: QZ issue attachments; physical Android HCI captures of one Tacx Neo 2
client: qdomyos-zwift (QZ), attributed by the submitter; not confirmed from the capture itself
evidenceTier: upstream hardware-observed evidence on one unit of unknown firmware; not FitBridge tier H
transport: Standard CPS 0x2A63 Cycling Power Measurement and CSC 0x2A5B CSC Measurement notifications from the Neo 2's own BLE services
why: The Neo 2 serves standard CPS and CSC alongside FE-C, and FitBridge has had no physical
corpus for either from a trainer. The value here is not the decoding, which is specified -
it is the awkward real-world shapes listed under hazards, every one of which is the kind of
thing a fixed-offset parser or a naive freshness rule gets wrong.

flagWordChangesMidStream.note: Both characteristics switch payload length mid-stream in BOTH directions - CPM between 10 and 14 octets as crank data appears and disappears, CSC between 7 and 11. Field offsets are not fixed across consecutive notifications on the same handle.

eventTimeRollover.note: uint16 event times in 1/2048 s wrap every 32 seconds and do so repeatedly here. A difference taken without unwrapping goes large and negative.

byteIdenticalConsecutiveRepeats.note: The trainer re-notifies unchanged packets at the notification rate rather than only on change. Over a third of the CPM stream is a byte-identical repeat of its predecessor, event time included. Any cumulative accumulation that adds deltas without checking identity, and any 'data is fresh because a packet arrived' rule, is wrong on this hardware.

hazards.cumulativeCountersDoNotResetWithinASessi: Wheel and crank revolution counters are monotonic within each session and restart across sessions; session 2 begins at wheel 1538, not zero, because it is a reconnect to a trainer that has been running.

expectations: Raw physical replay corpus. Decode with the CPS/CSC specifications and the production parsers; no mechanically generated decoded values are treated as goldens.
privacy: Only CPS and CSC measurement octets with session-relative timing. No addresses, device name, absolute timestamps or unrelated traffic. These characteristics carry no personal data.
